basis: How a damage curve earns a loss figure (E171). Stated before any test was run: a measured or published damage curve gives a published loss range only where it passed both tests below on losses it was not built from; otherwise the range is held (failed) or shown wide with the untested region named. The thresholds follow what the published evidence says curves can and cannot do: building-level damage is not predictable as a point (Wing et al. 2020: mean absolute error 84% of mean damage), so it is judged as a band; event totals can be (Hurricane Ike: USD 447.0m modelled against 450.0m recorded), so they are judged as totals.

measured_curves.depth_field_basis: FEMA: 'The depth of water, in inches, for a main building based on exterior water marks relative to the lowest adjacent grade' — the same reference as the JRC maps' water depth above ground. waterDepth is not used: FEMA notes some entries are in feet, and in the 219,532 claims holding both fields the median waterDepth/exteriorWaterDepth is 0.083 (= 1/12).

residential_codes.basis: FEMA occupancyType: 1 single family; 2 2–4 unit residential; 3 residential >4 units; 11 single-family residential; 12 residential non-condo 2–4 units; 13 residential non-condo 5+ units; 15 residential condo association; 16 single residential unit in a multi-unit building (mobile homes, 14, are not houses)

countries.added: 2026-10-23 (E322, the product owner's decision 'Log, guard, re-run')
countries.rule: a curve is built and tested from claims in the curve's countries only: FEMA's state field ("The two-character alpha abbreviation of the state in which the insured property is located") one of the 50 states or the District of Columbia (ISO 3166-2:US); Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands are ISO 3166-2:US outlying areas with their own ISO 3166-1 codes (PR, VI, GU, AS, MP), in the UN M49 regions of other curves, and a claim with no state cannot be placed — each set aside and counted
countries.found: until 2026-10-23 every value of the state field was read, so the measured family and published_curve_test took claims of PR, VI, GU, AS, MP and claims with no state into a US curve; the measured family is rebuilt under this rule and its first build kept under 'superseded'

test.held_out: each flood event with at least 500 claims is predicted from the other events' claims only

event_total.statement: predicted event total within ±30% of the recorded total in at least two thirds of the held-out events

band.statement: the 10th–90th percentile band holds between 75% and 85% of held-out claims (nominal 80%)

terrain_refinement.method: the JRC 1-in-100-year depth (90 m) re-spread over the Copernicus GLO-30 surface (30 m): in each wet 90 m pixel the water surface is the mean 30 m elevation of its land sub-pixels plus the mapped depth; a 30 m sub-pixel is wet where that surface stands more than 0.05 m above it. Water never spreads outside the pixels the JRC maps flood
terrain_refinement.target: the six Copernicus EMS observed flood extents of the flood_jrc_ems validator, on its own nodes (0.1° boxes inside each event box and the mapped area): the share of each box inside the observed extent
terrain_refinement.rule: the refinement is used only when, on the same nodes, BOTH its pooled Spearman rank correlation with the observed share AND its pooled AUC (observed share > 2%) are higher than the 90 m maps'; otherwise the 90 m maps stay and the result is recorded
terrain_refinement.statement: stated before the refinement was built or run

rule_from_2026_10_07.rule: for any refinement tested after this entry: used only when the 5th percentile of the paired-bootstrap difference (2,000 resamples of the nodes) is above zero for BOTH the rank correlation and the AUC — a gain inside sampling noise is not a gain
rule_from_2026_10_07.why: the first test (2026-10-06) met the original rule by +0.0015 in rank correlation and +0.0009 in AUC, with 90% intervals of the difference spanning zero; the original rule stays the one that test is judged by

building_scale_test.statement: stated before the building-scale test was built or run, at the product owner's request: the 0.1° node test cannot see a gain inside 90 m pixels, which is where the refinement claims one
building_scale_test.unit: each 30 m ground pixel (GLO-30 grid) on land, inside the area EMS mapped, within the flood_jrc_ems validator's judged nodes (at least half the box mapped) — the same six events and nodes
building_scale_test.observed: wet when the pixel's centre lies inside the EMS observed flooded extent
building_scale_test.predicted: wet at the 1-in-100-year period when the depth stands above 0.05 m — 90 m: the depth of the JRC pixel holding it; 30 m: the re-spread depth of terrain_refinement.method
building_scale_test.measure: Critical Success Index, CSI = hits / (hits + misses + false alarms), pooled over the events; hit rate and false-alarm ratio reported beside it, per event and pooled
building_scale_test.noise: paired block bootstrap: 2,000 resamples of the judged nodes (a node's pixels move together — neighbouring pixels are not independent), fixed seed
building_scale_test.rule: the refinement is better at building scale only when the 5th percentile of the resampled difference in pooled CSI (30 m minus 90 m) is above zero; when the 95th percentile is below zero it is worse; otherwise the test cannot tell them apart
building_scale_test.caveat_stated_before: a 1-in-100-year map is compared with single events larger or smaller than 1-in-100, which lowers both maps' CSI alike; the comparison between them is what the test reads, not either CSI on its own

projection_present_day_check.statement: stated before the check was built or run; it is reported, not a gate — the future cannot be tested, and this shows how far the projection source's present day sits from what was observed and from the JRC maps
projection_present_day_check.observed: the flood_jrc_ems validator's target and nodes: the six Copernicus EMS events, nodes at least half inside the mapped area, the observed flooded share of each node's mapped part
projection_present_day_check.predictor: as for the JRC maps: the share of the node box's 30″ pixels wet at the 1-in-100-year period × the depth–damage fraction at their mean depth (ml.scoring.flood_jrc.flood_score)
projection_present_day_check.measures: pooled Spearman rank correlation and AUC (observed share > 2%), beside the JRC maps' recorded run (ρ 0.68, AUC 0.80, 144 nodes)
projection_present_day_check.agreement: at every asset location: whether the two sources agree the place is wet or dry at the 1-in-100-year period (JRC: the location's H3 cell has a flooded share; Aqueduct: its 30″ pixel is wet), reported as counts

published_curve_test.statement: stated before the test was built or run, at the product owner's decision (2026-10-07): a published curve's figures are 'published' only after it passes this test; untested curves are shown as 'untested'
published_curve_test.claims: the same prepared NFIP claims and set-asides as measured_curves (residential codes, exteriorWaterDepth in inches, 0 < depth ≤ 144 in), depth converted to metres (× 0.0254)
published_curve_test.held_out: nothing is fitted to the claims, so every event with at least test.min_event_claims claims is held out
published_curve_test.predicted: each claim's damage ratio read off the curve at its depth (linear between the published points, the last held beyond); an event's predicted total = Σ ratio × the building's value (buildingPropertyValue)
published_curve_test.range: the curve's published range at each depth: the damage fraction ± one published standard deviation, bounded to [0, 1]
published_curve_test.pass: both of the protocol's tests as written in 'test': event totals within ±30% in at least two thirds of events (test.event_total), and the share of claims whose recorded damage ratio lies inside the range between 75% and 85% (test.band) — passed → published, failed → held
published_curve_test.note_stated_before: the band test was written for a 10th–90th percentile range; a ± one standard deviation range need not hold 75–85% of claims, and the test is applied as written all the same

corrected_2026_10_23.decided: the product owner's decision of 2026-10-23 ('Log, guard, re-run')
corrected_2026_10_23.found: the run of 2026-10-07 read the residential claims of every value of FEMA's state field — Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands and claims with no state among them — while the curve applies to the US (E322)
corrected_2026_10_23.correction: re-run on the claims in the curve's countries only: FEMA's state field ("The two-character alpha abbreviation of the state in which the insured property is located") one of the 50 states or the District of Columbia (ISO 3166-2:US); Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands are ISO 3166-2:US outlying areas with their own ISO 3166-1 codes (PR, VI, GU, AS, MP), in the UN M49 regions of other curves, and a claim with no state cannot be placed — each set aside and counted; everything else as registered. The claims and the curve were seen in the first run, so this corrects that run and is not a blind test; the first result is kept on the curve under 'superseded'

flood_protection.decided: the product owner's decisions of 2026-10-16: (1) protection levels from the JRC European map (jrc_flood_protection_europe); (2) the JRC European flood maps with nine return periods, once checked (europe_maps_check); (3) both figures shown — defended and undefended — and the institution states which leads (calc setting loss_flood_headline); (4) outside the protection map the undefended figure, labelled 'protection unknown'
flood_protection.rule: 'The flood protection is added to the risk curve as a vertical line. All impacts to the right of the flood protection line (i.e., damage from smaller floods) are assumed to be protected against and are set to 0. EAD is calculated by integrating the area of the curve to the left of the flood protection line.' and footnote 4: 'The flood protection, in return years, is first converted into a probability before being added to the calculation (i.e., 1/flood protection).' (Ward et al. 2020, Aqueduct Floods Methodology, section 6, p. 5 — data/datasets/sources/wri_aqueduct_floods_methodology_2020.pdf); the JRC's own PESETA IV assessment pairs this protection map with the same Huizinga et al. (2017) curves (Dottori et al. 2020, Annex A1.2)
flood_protection.applied_as: on the run's own loss–exceedance curve (straight lines in annual exceedance probability between the return periods held, the rarest loss held beyond the rarest): the line at p = 1 / design years; the curve's value at the line read on the same straight line; the defended expected annual loss is the area at probabilities at or below p, the same for the range's low and high curves. A line more frequent than the most frequent period held removes nothing (those floods are not in the maps); a line rarer than the rarest period held leaves only the held tail beyond the line

not_applied.projected runs: a defended projection is a named gap: the projection source moves the protection level with the climate ('a 50-year flood protection level in 2010 may only protect against 25-year floods in 2050', Ward et al. 2020, section 5), with its own protection data — not decided

europe_maps_check.statement: stated before the check was built or run
europe_maps_check.target: the flood_jrc_ems validator's six Copernicus EMS observed floods, on its own nodes (inside the event box, at least half the 0.1° box inside the area EMS mapped): the observed flooded share of each node's mapped part
europe_maps_check.predictor: for each map, as the validator reads the global maps: the share of the node box's land pixels flooded at the 1-in-100-year period (permanent water excluded, depths above 0.05 m) × the depth–damage fraction at their mean depth (ml.scoring.flood_jrc.flood_score)
europe_maps_check.rule: the European maps replace the global maps inside coverage_countries unless they rank the observed floods worse: refused when the 95th percentile of the paired-bootstrap difference (European − global; 2,000 resamples of the nodes, seed 7) is below zero for the rank correlation OR for the AUC (observed share > 2%)
europe_maps_check.why_not_better: the reason to switch is the nine return periods a defence level is read against (the product owner's decision, 2026-10-16), not a sharper flood extent — so the check guards against a worse map rather than demanding a better one

europe_loss_test.statement: stated before the test was built or run, at the product owner's decisions of 2026-10-20: (1) river floods only; (2) the years 1990–2020; (3) an event's loss split between its regions by their asset value in the river-flood zone; (4) each European curve tested on its own
europe_loss_test.question: do the flood losses the platform models for European regions rank like the river-flood losses those regions reported? It tests the whole chain — the European flood maps, the defence levels, one curve, and uniform exposure inside the flood zone — and cannot say which link fails

data.events: HANZE v2.1.1 (Paprotny et al. 2024, ESSD 16:5145; doi:10.5281/zenodo.8410025; CC BY 4.0): HANZE_events.csv, column 'Losses (2020 euro)' (direct tangible damage, inflation- and exchange-rate-adjusted by the authors), 'Regions affected (v2010)'
data.exposure: HANZE v2.0.3 exposure (Paprotny & Mengel 2023, Scientific Data 10; doi:10.5281/zenodo.7885990; CC BY 4.0): Exposure_river_hazard_zone.csv, 'Fixed assets (thsd. euro)', 50th percentile — the asset value inside each NUTS-3 region's riverine 1-in-100-year flood zone (the JRC pan-European 100-year map, Alfieri et al.), per timestep
data.regions: HANZE's NUTS-3 v2010 regions (Regions_v2010_simplified.zip, doi:10.5281/zenodo.8410025) — the codes the exposure uses and the events list as 'Regions affected (v2010)'

europe_loss_test.selection: events of Type 'River' or 'River/Coastal', Year 1990–2020 inclusive, with a value in 'Losses (2020 euro)'; regions in the countries the European maps cover (jrc_river_flood_europe coverage_countries) that the exposure file lists with zone assets above zero
europe_loss_test.observed: each selected event's loss is split between the regions it lists in proportion to each region's zone asset value in the event's year (the exposure's own timestep for that year, else the nearest earlier one); a region's observed rate = the sum of its shares ÷ 31 years ÷ the mean of its zone asset value over 1990–2020's timesteps; a region no selected event lists has an observed rate of 0
europe_loss_test.modelled: for each region and each curve: the region's flood zone is its cells (the European map's own, 3 arc-seconds, about 90 m) flooded in the European map's 1-in-100-year period — depth above 0.05 m, permanent water bodies neither land nor flooded, as the layer is read everywhere on the platform (jrc_river_flood_europe dry_basis); exposure is taken as spread evenly over those cells (no exposure grid is used); for each of the nine return periods the damage fraction is the mean over the zone's cells of the curve at that period's depth (0 where dry); a region's defence level is the median design return period of the protection map (jrc_flood_protection_europe) over its zone cells, and periods more frequent than it contribute 0 (the rule already registered in flood_protection, Ward et al. 2020); off the protection map the region is undefended; the expected annual damage fraction is the trapezoidal integral of the damage fraction over annual exceedance probability, as the engine integrates
europe_loss_test.metric: Spearman rank correlation, across the regions in scope, between the observed rate and the modelled expected annual damage fraction — one result per curve
europe_loss_test.rule: the platform's registered rank gate, unchanged (core/validation_gates, gates-v1): ρ ≥ RANK_GATE_SPEARMAN (0.35) with at least MIN_N_REGION_CLAIM regions; band monotonicity computed and reported, not a gate. Each curve's result is its own: passed → its European figures are shown as tested against reported regional losses (standing 'published'); failed → held
europe_loss_test.recorded: each result in the validation ledger (validation_run: kind rank, method out_of_sample — nothing is fitted to the losses — target the HANZE events above), and on the curve in its family file
europe_loss_test.limits_stated_before: reported losses under-count true damage (the authors estimate less than half before recent decades) and coverage differs by country (dense in Italy, Spain and France, sparse in Germany and the UK); losses mix all asset types while each curve is one building use; exposure is uniform inside the zone; the maps are today's hazard set against 31 years of events; a region with no reported event may still have had unreported losses. A pass says the chain ranks regions as reported losses do; a fail cannot say which link failed — the curve is held all the same, since its figures stand on the whole chain
europe_loss_test.amended_before_build: 2026-10-20, after registration (ec0654f) and before any code of the test was written or any figure computed: the registration said '100 m cells flooded (depth > 0)'. The map's cells are its own 3 arc-second grid (about 90 m), and a cell is flooded when its depth exceeds 0.05 m with permanent water excluded — the layer's registered reading, so the test reads the map as every other figure does. Nothing else changes.
europe_loss_test.amended_before_run: 2026-10-20, after the build and before any modelled figure was compared with a reported loss: the registration named the v2021 regions as 'the codes the events and the exposure use'. The exposure file uses HANZE's v2010 codes: on the events' v2021 lists, 188 listed regions had no asset value and 85 of the 369 selected events could not be split. The test now reads one region set throughout — the v2010 regions: the events' 'Regions affected (v2010)' (all 851 codes the selected events list are in the exposure), the exposure's own 1,422 codes, and HANZE's v2010 region outlines (Regions_v2010_simplified.zip, the same 1,422 codes; md5-verified). Nothing else changes.

us_storm_loss_test.statement: stated before the test was built or run, at the product owner's decisions of 2026-10-21: (1) wind damage decides pass or fail, and wind with storm-surge damage is shown beside it for information only; (2) each zone's damage is divided by its asset value from LitPop, the exposure the curves were calibrated with; (3) each US curve is tested on its own; (4) the forecast zones of the Atlantic and Gulf coast states; (5) damage converted to one year's dollars with the US consumer price index
us_storm_loss_test.question: do the tropical-cyclone wind losses the platform models for US forecast zones rank like the wind damage those zones reported? It tests the whole chain — the STORM wind maps, their reading as 1-minute wind (÷ 0.88), one curve, and LitPop's spread of assets — and cannot say which link fails

data.damage: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database, details files 1996–2025 (data/loss_val/noaa_storm_events; ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/swdi/stormevents/csvfiles): wind = EVENT_TYPE 'Hurricane (Typhoon)', 'Hurricane' and 'Tropical Storm'; 'Storm Surge/Tide' is added only for the information figure; DAMAGE_PROPERTY as recorded (K thousand, M million, B billion), in the dollars of the record's year
data.zones: NWS public forecast zones as of 18 March 2025 (z_18mr25, data/windstorm_val/nws_zones.zip): a record is placed in the zone its STATE and CZ_FIPS name (CZ_TYPE 'Z'); a record by county (CZ_TYPE 'C'), or naming a zone the 2025 outlines no longer hold, is counted and set aside
data.exposure: LitPop_150arcsec_USA.hdf5 (CLIMADA data API, dataset version v3, CC BY 4.0, md5 9f019394e1736e67c6fd5572875a2fa1; Eberenz et al. 2020, ESSD 12:817): produced capital (reference year 2018) spread in proportion to nightlight × population, 150 arc-seconds; a zone's asset value is the sum of the values of the cells whose centres fall in its outline
data.prices: BLS CPI-U, all items, US city average (series CUUR0000SA0), monthly indexes 1996–2025 from the BLS Public Data API (data/datasets/bls_cpi_u, three replies, sha-256 recorded with the result)
data.states: the Atlantic and Gulf coast states of NOAA Office for Coastal Management's 'Shoreline Mileage of the United States' (coast.noaa.gov/data/docs/states/shorelines.pdf; data/datasets/noaa_shoreline, sha-256 c58e3e52…): AL, CT, DE, FL, GA, LA, ME, MD, MA, MS, NH, NJ, NY, NC, PA, RI, SC, TX, VA — Texas to Maine; Pennsylvania for its tidal Delaware River shoreline, which the table counts; New York whole, though part of its shoreline is on the Great Lakes
data.files_verified: LitPop md5 against the CLIMADA data API, 2026-10-21; the other files fingerprinted on receipt

us_storm_loss_test.selection: the forecast zones of the listed states whose LitPop asset value is above zero; the years 1996–2025 (2026 is incomplete)
us_storm_loss_test.observed: each wind record's damage converted to 2024 dollars by the ratio of CPI-U yearly averages (2024's ÷ the record's year's; a yearly average is the mean of the year's twelve monthly indexes, computed here because the free API publishes none; 2024 is the last year with all twelve — BLS footnotes October 2025 'Data unavailable due to the 2025 lapse in appropriations' — and a damage record in a year without twelve indexes stops the run); summed per zone, ÷ 30 years ÷ the zone's asset value; a zone with no record has a rate of 0
us_storm_loss_test.modelled: for each zone and curve: at each LitPop cell centre in the zone, the storm_v4_wind layer's wind at its eight return periods (services.loss.storm_events.rows, as every storm figure reads it), divided by 0.88 (the layer's registered reading for 1-minute wind); the curve's damage ratio at each return period (services.loss.curves.ratio); the expected annual damage ratio by the engine's trapezoid (services.loss.engine.eal); the zone's figure is the asset-weighted mean over its cells
us_storm_loss_test.metric: Spearman rank correlation, across the zones in scope, between the observed rate and the modelled expected annual damage ratio — one result per curve
us_storm_loss_test.information: beside each result, the same correlation with wind and storm-surge damage together ('Storm Surge/Tide' records added); shown for information, not gated, changing no standing
us_storm_loss_test.rule: the platform's registered rank gate, unchanged (core/validation_gates, gates-v1): ρ ≥ RANK_GATE_SPEARMAN (0.35) with at least MIN_N_REGION_CLAIM zones; band monotonicity computed and reported, not a gate. Each curve's result is its own: passed → its figures (USA and Canada, the curve's region) are shown as tested against reported zone damage (standing 'published'); failed → held
us_storm_loss_test.recorded: each result in the validation ledger (validation_run: hazard 'cyclone_loss', read as the tropical-cyclone channel; kind rank; method out_of_sample — nothing is fitted to these losses) and on the curve in its family file
us_storm_loss_test.independence: the curves were calibrated on EM-DAT's reported damage per event and country, 1980–2017 (Eberenz et al. 2021); this test ranks forecast zones inside the US, which the calibration never saw, but the US event totals behind EM-DAT and NOAA overlap — stated, not removed
us_storm_loss_test.limits_stated_before: NOAA damage figures are the National Weather Service's estimates and are incomplete; a 'Hurricane' record may still carry some water damage; zone outlines of 2025 against 30 years of records; LitPop's 2018 assets against the calibration's 2014 and against 30 years of events; the STORM maps are a long-run climate set against 30 observed years, so a zone the model rates highly may simply not have been hit; Canada is in the curve's region but not in the test. A pass says the chain ranks zones as reported damage does; a fail cannot say which link failed — the curve is held all the same, since its figures stand on the whole chain
us_storm_loss_test.amended_before_run: 2026-10-21, after registration (ce7b572) and before any modelled figure was compared with reported damage, at the product owner's decision of the same day: the unit is the NWS forecast office area, not the forecast zone. The registration placed a record in the zone its STATE and CZ_FIPS name on the 18 March 2025 outlines; the build's input check found that $92.7bn of the $238.0bn of wind damage (2024 dollars, 39%) is recorded in zone codes those outlines no longer hold — zones NWS split or renamed, mostly in the 2004–2005 and 2020 seasons — and a match on the same state and zone name recovers 6% of it. Every record names its forecast office (WFO), and the 2025 outlines name each zone's office (CWA), which places 99.9% of the damage. So: a record of the listed states, by zone or by county, is placed in the office area its WFO names; an office area is the 2025 outlines' zones of that office within the listed states; its asset value is the LitPop value of the cells whose centres fall in those zones; a record naming an office the 2025 outlines do not hold ('EYW', $0.21bn) is counted and set aside. Everything else — damage, prices, exposure, the modelled figure (now the asset-weighted mean over the office area's cells), the curves, the metric, the rule and the information figure — is unchanged, with 'zone' read as 'office area'. Also found and fixed before any figure was computed: NOAA writes some amounts without a leading zero ('.5M', '.2B') and the first parser set them aside (E305).

published_curve_test_commercial.statement: stated before the test was built or run, at the product owner's decisions of 2026-10-23: (1) 'Commercial only' — the North America commercial curve is tested on NFIP claims of non-residential buildings, mobile homes left out as for houses; the North America industrial curve stays untested, as FEMA's occupancy codes do not separate industrial buildings; (2) 'Event-total test alone' — the curve publishes no range, so the event-total test decides alone
published_curve_test_commercial.why_this_data: a curve's level is judged only by records that give, per building, the water depth, the damage in money and the building's value; the search of 2026-10-23 for such records under an open licence found none in Europe (docs/GO_LIVE_EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCIES.md, item 19) and, outside the US, none with enough claims; the NFIP claims already held give all three for non-residential buildings
published_curve_test_commercial.claims: the prepared NFIP claims (services.loss.claims) of FEMA occupancyType 4 'Non-residential building', 6 'Non Residential - Business', 18 'A non-residential building' and 19 'a non-residential unit within a multi-unit building' (NFIP Redacted Claims v3 data dictionary); 17 'Non-residential mobile/manufactured home' left out, as mobile homes (14) are left out of the houses; in the curve's countries only: FEMA's state field ("The two-character alpha abbreviation of the state in which the insured property is located") one of the 50 states or the District of Columbia (ISO 3166-2:US); Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands are ISO 3166-2:US outlying areas with their own ISO 3166-1 codes (PR, VI, GU, AS, MP), in the UN M49 regions of other curves, and a claim with no state cannot be placed — each set aside and counted; exteriorWaterDepth in inches with measured_curves' set-asides (no exterior depth, the 999 placeholder, zero or below, above 144 inches), converted to metres (× 0.0254)
published_curve_test_commercial.held_out: nothing is fitted to the claims, so every event with at least test.min_event_claims claims is held out
published_curve_test_commercial.predicted: as published_curve_test: each claim's damage ratio read off the curve at its depth (linear between the published points, the last held beyond); an event's predicted total = Σ ratio × the building's value (buildingPropertyValue)
published_curve_test_commercial.range: none: the workbook publishes no standard deviation for this curve (its 'spread': 'none published'), so the range test of test.band has nothing to judge and is recorded as not applicable
published_curve_test_commercial.pass: the event-total test as written in test.event_total, alone: the predicted event total within ±30% of the recorded total in at least two thirds of the held-out events — passed → published (its US figures shown as tested), failed → held
published_curve_test_commercial.recorded: on the curve in its family file, as published_curve_test
published_curve_test_commercial.seen_before: before this registration only counts were made, with no curve: on the raw claims file, 24,164 claims of codes 4, 6, 18 and 19 in the 50 states and DC with an exterior depth above 0 and at most 144 inches, a building value above zero and a damage amount, 9 events with at least 500 of them (11,997 claims); the prepared file's own set-asides (no recorded waterDepth, damage above the building's value) may lower them
published_curve_test_commercial.limits_stated_before: NFIP records insured buildings only, valued at the adjuster's actual cash value (as for the houses); 'non-residential' mixes shops, offices, warehouses, places of worship and farm buildings, while the curve is the commercial one; the buildings are those insured in the US while the curve speaks for North America; the North America residential curve failed this test by over-predicting every event (2026-10-07). A pass says the curve's event totals stand within the tolerance on these claims; a fail holds the curve
